overview: Lapita names an archaeological tradition recognised especially through distinctive pottery across parts of the Pacific. It should not be drawn as one kingdom or treated as an identical society at every site.

items.text: Potters impressed wet clay with small toothed tools before firing. Repeated elements combined into elaborate geometric compositions.
Some ceramic designs include faces or human figures. Excavated objects also include freestanding human and animal forms.
Large vessels have been interpreted as containers for preparing, serving or storing food. These functions are interpretations, not labels preserved by their makers.
Many Lapita-associated settlements occupied coasts, and ocean travel connected dispersed islands. Individual routes and settlement dates need site-specific evidence.

sources.title: Jennifer Wagelie, Lapita Pottery
sources.note: Ceramic design, manufacture and interpreted vessel functions; 2002 essay, chronology requires newer primary research
